findings.title: GET /tasks NULLS handling for due_date sort under asc/desc is not fully specified
findings.location: REST API > GET /tasks; Edge Cases > sort by nullable priority/due_date
findings.problem: NULLS placement is stated for priority but not pinned for due_date across both order=asc and order=desc; SQL default differs (NULLS FIRST for ASC), yielding two valid interpretations.
findings.fix: State one rule for all sort columns and both orders and give the exact template: ORDER BY <sortcol> <order> NULLS LAST, id <order>.

findings.title: GET /tasks id tie-break direction is unspecified; risks ORDER BY drift across pages
findings.location: REST API > GET /tasks (vs GET /projects which fixes id DESC)
findings.problem: GET /tasks says 'tie-break by id appended to every sort' without fixing direction, so the data query and any re-query could differ.
findings.fix: Pin the tie-break to follow order (, id <order>) and declare it the single authoritative ORDER BY form reused across pages.

findings.title: Task response object shape is never defined
findings.location: REST API > POST/GET/PATCH /tasks and GET /tasks/:id (all return { task: {...} })
findings.problem: The task payload field list is enumerated nowhere, unlike user/project/member/attachment. Implementer must guess fields and whether joins are embedded.
findings.fix: Define a canonical task shape { id, title, description, status, priority, due_date, creator_id, assignee_id, project_id, created_at, updated_at } and require all task endpoints to return it identically.

findings.title: Comment, notification, and notification.payload shapes are undefined
findings.problem: { comment } and { notification } field lists and the JSONB payload 'task snapshot' keys are never specified, so REST responses and the socket event have no fixed contract.
findings.fix: Enumerate comment { id, task_id, author_id, body, created_at }, notification { id, user_id, type, payload, read, created_at }, and the payload keys (e.g. { task_id, title, status, project_id, actor_id }).

findings.title: GET /tasks assignee/project filter semantics vs authz not stated, inviting an incorrect extra authz check
findings.location: REST API > GET /tasks visibility+filter SQL and trailing paragraph
findings.problem: The doc does not state that assignee/project filters are pure AND narrowings of the base predicate; an implementer could wrongly add a 403/404 for a filter value the caller cannot otherwise see.
findings.fix: Add: 'the assignee and project filters are pure AND narrowings of the base visibility predicate; an unseen filter value simply yields fewer/zero rows and is never itself an authorization error.'

findings.title: Logout/blocklist expired-token note
findings.problem: Logout is only reachable with a still-valid token, so the blocklist never stores already-expired exp; this is correct but implicit.
findings.fix: Add one clarifying sentence; no behavioral change.

findings.title: 'Exactly one of user_id | email' needs an explicit zod refine
findings.problem: The exactly-one cross-field rule is not expressible via plain z.object and the schema shape is not pinned.
findings.fix: Specify z.object({...}).refine(d => (d.user_id == null) !== (d.email == null), 'provide exactly one of user_id or email') and 400 on both-or-neither.

findings.title: PATCH /notifications/:id should use z.literal(true), not z.boolean()
findings.problem: Body is fixed to { read: true }; using z.boolean() would silently accept false and no-op.

findings.title: due_date datetime vs date-only input semantics unstated
findings.location: tasks table; POST /tasks due_date?: ISO datetime
findings.problem: Validator requires full ISO datetime, so a date-only due date would 400; time-of-day semantics are not documented.
findings.fix: Either accept date-only and coerce to end-of-day UTC, or document that a full ISO datetime is required; pick one explicitly.
